sections.title: 阅读 A · Tony Buzan 的书单
passage: If you like the idea of being able to read much faster, remember more easily, and being more creative, this list of Tony Buzan's books might be inspirational to get you started.
Study Skills Handbook This book does not focus only on reading efficiency but also covers the subjects of memory improvement and mind mapping. It is an absolute must for students of all ages.

Speed Reading This popular book explains the principles of efficient reading. It allows you to improve your reading and retention (记忆力) skills immediately. The book gets right down to the practical matter of reading.

The Mind Map Book The Mind Map Book is a ground-breaking work on the basics of mind mapping suitable for everyone and introduces revolutionary techniques for planning and note-taking. It is one of Tony Buzan's books that has sold over 10 million copies.

Use Your Head Use Your Head is for those of you that feel as if you have not been able to reach your full potential. In this book, Tony Buzan teaches you how to think and learn from all possible sources of learning.

sections.title: 阅读 B · Bike Batman
passage: Bike Batman is a 31-year-old married engineer who lives in Seattle, Washington. He's a cyclist who also buys and sells bikes as a hobby.

About three years ago, he was looking for a bike for his wife. He found one on Craigslist, a website where people list things they want to sell. As he often did, he also looked at Bike Index, a popular site where stolen bikes are recorded.

After that first success, Bike Batman developed a safer routine. When he sees questionable bike ads on Craigslist, he cross-references the image with bikes reported on Bike Index. Once he has checked the bike is listed as stolen, he contacts the owner and helps him recover it.

His nickname came from a discussion with a police officer who suggested he be called “Robin Hood”. Since he wasn't exactly stealing from the rich and giving to the poor, “Batman” seemed a better nickname.

questions.stem: What will Bike Batman first do when discovering a questionable bike?

frags.t: He'll contact the real bike owner.
He'll arrange to meet the thief.
He'll look up the bike's information.

frags.t: The thieves refused to return the bikes.

sections.title: 阅读 C · 父母 influence 与大学选择
passage: When you're in high school, deciding what you'd like to study at college is not always easy. We may choose to balance (平衡) our own hopes and dreams with those of our parents, as well as think about what our friends are doing.

Researchers from South Korea have been trying to find out the influence that conversations with parents have on high school students' course choices. And they think they might have found a pattern (模式).

The researchers looked at information of almost 1,300 students who were in the second year of high school in 2016, and followed them as they moved on to college. They found that students who often talked with their parents about college were more likely to consider a range of options.

The research team said that South Korean parents were now having more of an influence on their children's choices about college. “Talking with parents greatly influences students' decisions on what to study,” said the team.

But there were other important factors (因素), too. Children with richer parents were more likely to go to college, and students with higher grades in math were also more likely to go to college. But parents' talk was still the single biggest factor they found.

questions.stem: What can we learn from the study?

frags.t: Choosing a college is usually hard for children.
Children should spend more time with parents.
Children refuse to share their dreams with their parents.
Communication with parents is influential in children's decisions.

questions.stem: How did the researchers carry out their study?

frags.t: Parents Help Students Make Better Choices

sections.title: 阅读 D · 方便面到底算不算垃圾食品
passage: Instant noodles are a favorite quick meal when people don't want to cook. Picture eating them while watching TV on a stormy night — pure comfort! But many believe they're just junk food that harms your health.

The main issue isn't the noodles themselves, but the common way people make them: pouring boiling water over dried noodles and adding all the salty seasoning packets. These flavor packets contain high amounts of sodium (钠).

Actually, plain instant noodles aren't terrible. They're fried during production (which adds some oil and calories), but they fill you up well and provide quick energy when you're hungry. To make them healthier, use less seasoning and add vegetables and protein.

So, are instant noodles junk food? If prepared lazily with all the seasoning and no extras, yes. But when cooked with less seasoning plus veggies and protein, they become a decent occasional meal. Remember, it's all about balance.

questions.stem: What determines if instant noodles are unhealthy?

sections.hint: 以下两题为主观题，提交后可对照参考答案自评。

writing.title: 应用文写作 · 我的高中初体验
writing.stem:
请以“我的高中初体验”为题，写一篇短文。内容包括：
（1）结合开学首日印象完成自我介绍（不得出现真实名字）；
（2）点明一个开学第一周面临的巨大挑战并描述自己是如何应对这个挑战的。
writing.note: 词数 120；内容凝练，情感真实。
writing.ref:
My first taste of senior high school

My first taste of senior high school arrived on the opening day. Standing among crowds of new faces, I felt nervous but excited. I am an easy-going person, eager to make new friends and explore new knowledge.

The biggest challenge in the first week was keeping up with the fast pace of lessons. There was much more knowledge to take in than in junior high. Instead of feeling upset, I made a simple plan. I set aside half an hour every evening to review and to ask questions in class.

Little by little, I adapted to the new life. I believe with efforts, I will make progress in senior high.

writing.title: 读后续写 · 意外涂红的模型车
writing.stem: 阅读下面材料，根据其内容和所给段落首句续写两段，使之构成一篇完整的短文。
material: Ethan enjoyed riding the school bus home. The ride home gave him some time to relax after a busy day of fifth grade. He usually sat alone and enjoyed that too. With four siblings, he didn't get much attention at home.

The bus stopped and the tallest boy in his class, Troy, stepped off followed by his younger brother, Jamie. As the bus pulled away, Ethan looked back over his shoulder to watch the boys. Troy was yelling at Jamie and pushing him.
Ethan turned in his seat, feeling disgusted. He hated seeing little kids get picked on. The sight of Jamie on the ground crying was burned into his memory. He tried to think of something else.

He thought of the model car he was working on at home, a 1967 Corvette. He started building it over a week ago and just finished putting it together last night. Tonight, as soon as he finished his homework, he was going to paint it.

He hurried off the bus, ran through his yard, and breezed through the kitchen with a quick hello to his mom. She was making spaghetti, which smelled delicious. He ran up the stairs two at a time and reached his room.
“Surprise!” his brother Lucas said, throwing his arms into the air. “What are you doing in my room? I thought you were sick!”
“What's on your face? Are you bleeding?”
“No! I'm not bleeding.” Lucas wiped at his face. “It's probably just paint. Look! Look what I did!” He pointed at the desk in the corner of Ethan's room.
starts: Ethan looked down at his desk in horror.
Ethan took a deep breath and then unfolded his fist.
writing.note: 续写词数 150 左右；按所给段落首句续写。
writing.ref:
（参考）Ethan looked down at his desk in horror. His Corvette! Lucas had painted it red — an awful dull shade of red. “Why would you do that?” Ethan shouted. “I wanted to surprise you!” Lucas grinned.

Ethan took a deep breath and then unfolded his fist. Picturing the scene that Jamie sat on the ground wiping at his eyes, Ethan stepped toward the table. He took the brush, dipped it in the blue paint, and began to cover the red — covering, he thought, his own anger.
